decisions.location: Claim evaluations, Claim ID: gkzl8g, Discussion (lines 328-342)
decisions.reason: Row 1389 (work_key 10.17605/osf.io/w8n3s, target Axt, Moran, & Bar-Anan, 2018) evaluates 13 focal claims across Studies 1-5. Under the codebook's central-finding rule ('Both axes concern the central finding this paper set out to check, not incidental or exploratory analyses around it'), all 13 claims are the explicit target findings the paper set out to evaluate ('Push Button Reproduction Attempt to Evaluate 13 Claims from Axt_JournExpSocPsych_2018_zK2'), and within Claim gkzl8g, the effect size is listed under 'Primary reproduction criteria' as the 'Focal effect size' of the claim rather than an incidental or exploratory analysis. For Claim gkzl8g, the original paper reported a focal effect size of d = -0.51, whereas re-running the analysis on the original data produced d = -0.60, which falls outside even the report's approximate reproduction interval (d = -0.59 to -0.43) into the non-reproduction range (< -0.59 or > -0.43), and the analyst explicitly states: 'The focal effect size (d=-0.60) did not reproduce.' (In addition, Study 4 claims g7opxm, bz28qb, and glzvdm achieved only approximate reproduction of reported sample sizes, and Claims bdj1jb and m7475m achieved only approximate reproduction of t and d.) While the analyst marks all 13 claims as reproduced under the SCORE 'Analyst success criteria', the text explicitly defines that criterion as 'precise reproduction of the primary outcome p-value' rather than recovery of the reported numbers. Codebook Axis 1 (outcome_computation) asks 'did re-running the analysis produce the original numbers? Only the numbers matter here' and instructs coders to work through the categories in order and stop at the first that fits: item 3 ('computational issues') applies when 'the analysis ran and produced numbers, but the reported numbers were not obtained: coefficients differed, results could not be recovered, or the paper reports discrepancies it treats as substantive,' whereas item 4 ('computationally reproducible') is limited to cases where 'the reported numbers were obtained again' with only 'Rounding and negligible numerical differences.' Settling Axis 1 over the evaluated claims together and following the analyst's own explicit judgment that the focal effect size d = -0.51 (reproduced as d = -0.60) 'did not reproduce', the correct coding is 'computational issues'.

scope_review.parent_objection: Claim gkzl8g reports original focal d=-0.51 but reproduced d=-0.60, outside even the report's approximate range, and states that the focal effect size did not reproduce. All primary p-values and most statistics reproduce. The prior review calls the axis computationally reproducible based on primary-p-value success criteria. Decide independently whether that disregards a substantive reported-number discrepancy under the codebook. Do not equate SCORE success with numerical recovery automatically; also consider whether the disputed number is central or incidental. Address these exact values and the central-finding rule explicitly.
